newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-SFE May wheat falls A$2.00 in lone trade.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-SFE May wheat falls A$2.00 in lone trade.

text.p: Nearby May wheat settled A$2.00 lower at A$160.00 a tonne in Sydney Future Exchange trading on Thursday that saw only one lot traded across the board.

Futures traders largely ignored the potential of higher Australian wheat sales emerging from concern over the extent of damage to Argentina's wheat crop and cold weather in the U.S. winter wheat growing region.
Instead they continued to focus on expectations that Australia will harvest a record or near record harvest approaching 22 million tonnes.

Some commodities traders have said they believe the storms that have wreaked havoc on Argentina's wheat crop may end up boosting world wheat prices and force East Asian buyers to turn to other suppliers like Canada or Australia.
One Australian trader said he understood the heaviest rains may have fallen on young crop, which in the long term could boost wheat production.
Estimates in Australia are running at damage to crops estimated at anywhere between 300,000 tonnes to one million tonnes.
